note: Traded-player exceptions the trackers carry at the wrong amount, keyed by team and player. scrape-tpes.mjs applies these after it reconciles Spotrac's and SalarySwish's lists, so a re-pull keeps the correction; remove an entry once both trackers agree with it. Each entry says what they print, what the CBA makes it, and why.

corrections.why: Oklahoma City sent Wiggins to Atlanta on Jul 6 for two seconds, creating an exception of his Salary. Both trackers print $9,224,300, which is his base ($8,831,776) plus BOTH bonuses — but Art. VII §3(d) excludes unlikely bonuses from Salary, so the exception is base plus the $196,262 likely bonus: $9,028,038, the cap hit Spotrac's own Thunder and Hawks pages carry.

Atlanta absorbed Wiggins into its $11,000,000 Kennard exception. Spotrac's exception page and its Hawks page leave $1,971,962 (11,000,000 less his $9,028,038 Salary); SalarySwish leaves $1,775,700, subtracting his unlikely bonus too, which §3(d) keeps out of Salary. The scraper had resolved to SalarySwish.
